D007-D005_h001.question:
I’ve been having these…episodes for about six months now. It started with this absolute certainty that my ex-partner is seeing someone else behind my back, even though we split years ago and barely speak. I still check his social media, watch who he “likes,” and I *know* there’s someone he’s hiding, even though everyone tells me I’m being irrational. It feels as real as the books on my shelves.

Around the same time, I began seeing people in the library after closing—figures standing between the stacks, sometimes children sitting in the reading room. When I walk closer, they’re gone. I also see shapes moving in my flat, like someone just stepped out of the corner of my eye.

My staff complain I’m “hard to follow.” When they ask a simple question about scheduling, I start talking about cataloguing systems or a book I read, and then I lose track of what they actually asked.

For about a month in the middle of all this, I felt oddly hollow—nothing excited me, not even finishing a big archive project. I slept normal hours but woke up exhausted, pacing my flat or picking at my hands, unable to sit still. That heavy, flat feeling has mostly lifted now, but the suspicions and the figures I see have kept going.
D007-D005_h001.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    D. Persistent Depressive Disorder

D007-D005_h002.question:
I’ve been feeling “off” for maybe seven months now. At first it was mostly this heavy, low feeling. I’m just…down all the time. I used to joke with the other guys at the building and have coffee with them, but lately I keep to myself in the basement or go straight home. My wife says I barely talk. Even walking my rounds feels like I’m moving through mud; I’m slower, clumsier. At night I lie there for hours before I can fall asleep, just staring at the ceiling.

About a month into feeling depressed, the stranger stuff started and hasn’t let up these past six months. I’m convinced something terrible is coming, like the world is hollowing out from the inside and will just collapse any day. It doesn’t feel like a “worry,” it feels like a fact. I also get these crawling sensations on my arms and back, like bugs under the skin, but there’s never anything there.

Sometimes when I talk, my wife looks confused. I catch myself using words like “dustfall” and “skin-sparks” that make perfect sense to me, but she says they’re not real words.
D007-D005_h002.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    D. Persistent Depressive Disorder

D007-D005_h003.question:
It started around seven months ago with me just feeling low all the time. Not crying, exactly, but sort of emotionally flat and heavy. Things I used to enjoy—sketching, model-making, even going out to look at buildings—just felt pointless. I was dragging at work, taking forever to answer clients’ questions because my thoughts felt slowed down and my speech got…sticky, like I had to push the words out. I’d sleep eight, nine hours and still wake up exhausted, like the sleep didn’t “take.”

About a month after that, the stranger stuff began and has pretty much dominated since. For the past six months I’ve been convinced this actress I follow online is sending me secret messages—that she’s secretly in love with me. I can explain the patterns in her posts and interviews; it all fits, to me at least. Around the same time I started smelling this faint perfume scent or sometimes smoke when no one else could smell anything. It happens in my apartment and at the office.

Lately my words sometimes get tangled—“design, align, refine, divine”—I catch myself rhyming or chaining sounds instead of answering directly. Work has fallen apart; I’ve missed deadlines, and my firm pulled me off two projects. The low mood comes and goes now, but the beliefs and odd smells haven’t really let up.
D007-D005_h003.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    D. Persistent Depressive Disorder

D007-D005_h004.question:
I’ve been struggling for about six, seven months now. The thing that scares me most is this feeling that something is really wrong inside my body. I’m convinced there’s some kind of infection or rot in my organs that nobody is catching, even though all my tests at work and at urgent care have come back “normal.” It doesn’t feel normal. I can smell it on myself sometimes, like this faint rotting or chemical smell, especially when I’m alone at home or in the exam rooms at the clinic, but no one else seems to notice it.

Talking about it, I know I jump around a lot—I'll be telling you about a dog I’m restraining and then suddenly I'm onto how the lights in the surgery room feel like they’re burning my skin and then I’m back to the smell again. My coworkers say I’m hard to follow.

For a couple of weeks here and there during these months, I’ve also been really down—crying in the break room, not caring about my usual stuff like hiking or watching vet videos, waking up at 2 or 3 a.m. and pacing around my apartment, picking at my hands until they’re raw. But those really low spells come and go; the weird body stuff and smells have been constant.
D007-D005_h004.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    D. Persistent Depressive Disorder

D007-D005_h005.question:
It’s been about six months now that things have felt…off. At first I thought it was just the stress of my account blowing up and all the hate online, but this is different.  

I’m completely convinced this one big-name musician is secretly in love with me. I “see” hints in his lyrics, his posts, even the colors he wears. I know people say it’s coincidence, but it feels like he’s sending me messages. Sometimes I even see him, or other people, in my apartment or outside my window—like full figures—then I blink and they’re gone.  

When I talk, my mind jumps tracks. I’ll start telling my manager about a brand deal and suddenly I’m talking about my neighbor’s dog or the shape of clouds, and I don’t really notice until people look confused. That’s been going on most of these six months.  

I did go through a really low period for maybe a few weeks—felt empty, stopped enjoying posting, slept most of the day, moved like my body was heavy—but that kind of faded. The weird beliefs and seeing things never really stopped, even when my mood wasn’t that low.

    C. Body Dysmorphic Disorder

D007-D005_h006.question:
It started about a year and a half ago with this fixed idea that everything is heading toward some kind of collapse. It’s not like a political worry; it feels absolutely certain, like I “know” the world is about to end and all my landscape plans are pointless because nothing will be here. That thought is there pretty much every day now, even when I’m at a job site talking about drainage or plant lists.

Around the same time I began getting these strange tastes in my mouth, like metal or rotten food, out of nowhere, even when I’m not eating. Sometimes it feels like someone has poisoned my food, so I avoid office snacks or skip lunch on site. When I’m trying to explain designs to clients, my thoughts jump tracks mid-sentence and I’ll suddenly start talking about something unrelated, like flooding or extinction, and people look confused. My husband says I “lose the thread” a lot.

The really flat, empty, guilty feelings came a bit later and were worst for a few months straight; I could barely enjoy anything, lost my appetite, and felt somehow to blame for disasters I heard about on the news. That part has eased up somewhat, but the sense that catastrophe is imminent and the bad tastes and jumbled talking have just kept going.
D007-D005_h006.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Body Dysmorphic Disorder

D007-D005_h007.question:

I’d come home from visits with families and instead of venting to my husband, I’d just sit on the couch staring. I stopped wanting to see friends, stopped returning calls. Over a few weeks I dropped nearly a stone without trying because I just couldn’t be bothered to eat. I became convinced that every bad outcome in my cases was somehow my fault, even things I wasn’t involved in. I still kind of feel that way, like I’m responsible for kids getting hurt on the other side of the city.

About four or five months after that, things changed in a different way. For the last year and a bit I’ve been sure people are watching me—colleagues, social services, maybe even the council—tracking what I do. I see shadows of people in my house or in the office who disappear when I try to focus on them. When I talk, I start trying to explain this and then my mind slips off onto something else and I lose the thread. The low mood comes and goes now, but these other things have just kept going and taken over my life and my work.
D007-D005_h007.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Body Dysmorphic Disorder

D007-D005_h008.question:

I stopped caring about things I used to enjoy, like trying new recipes or chatting with regulars at the restaurant.     C. Persistent Depressive Disorder

D007-D005_h009.question:

I used to love planning campaigns and making content, and even just scrolling for fun, but for the last year and seven months I’ve felt like I’m just going through the motions. I’ve put on a lot of weight in a short time because I just sit and snack, but I don’t even care much—everything feels distant, like I’m watching my own life from the outside.

When I talk, my mind jumps—I'll start about work, then suddenly I’m talking about satellites or my old high school without realizing how I got there. D007-D005_h010.question:

Like, when I scroll through comments on my webtoon or see random posts on social media, I feel like they’re secretly directed at me, hinting at something I’m supposed to understand. Even people talking on the subway, or the way someone clears their throat, feels like it’s coded toward me. It’s not just once in a while; it’s become kind of my default way of reading the world.

Around that same time, I started smelling things that no one else seems to notice—like a strong burning plastic or rotten smell in my room even when nothing’s there. It distracts me when I’m trying to draw, especially late at night before deadlines.

Sometimes when people ask me something, like my editor on a call, I start answering but drift off and end up talking about completely different things, like my drawing process or some random scene idea, and only later realize I never actually answered what they asked.

The low mood stuff has come and gone during this period—maybe a few weeks at a time where I just feel hollow, like I’m on autopilot. During those times, even hitting big milestones, like a spike in subscribers or fan messages, doesn’t move me at all. I eat more then—snacking all day at my desk—and I get stuck thinking my work is pointless, that I’m pointless. But those heavier, empty phases aren’t constant; they kind of fade, then come back, while the weirdness with smells and feeling like everything is about me has been more steady throughout.
D007-D005_h010.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Body Dysmorphic Disorder

D007-D005_h011.question:
It started about seven months ago on the rig. At first it was the voices. I’ll be checking gauges in the engine room and hear someone right behind me, clear as day, saying stuff like, “It’s coming, everything’s going to be wiped out,” or calling my name and telling me the sea will swallow us. I look around and there’s no one there. I’ve also become convinced something huge is about to destroy everything, like the world is already kind of over and we’re just walking around in the ruins. It doesn’t feel like a thought, it feels like a fact.

Talking is getting harder. My words get all jumbled, like my mouth runs ahead of my brain and I can’t string a normal sentence together. The guys at work stare at me like they don’t know what I’m saying. I find myself doing weird little things with my hands, like tapping out patterns on the rail or saluting the cranes every time I pass them, and I can’t really explain why.

I mostly keep to myself now—skip calls home, avoid the crew in the mess. For a short spell a few months back, I got really low on top of this—nothing felt enjoyable, I paced nonstop in my cabin, picked at my skin, kept thinking every mistake on the rig was my fault and that maybe everyone would be better off if I wasn’t around. Those feelings eased up some, but the voices and the end-of-the-world stuff never really let up.
D007-D005_h011.options:
A. Anorexia Nervosa
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia

D007-D005_h012.question:
I sell houses, or I used to, but for about seven months my mind has been…broken, I guess. It started with this certainty that everything is about to be wiped out. There was a stretch — maybe a few weeks in the middle of all this — where I also felt incredibly slow and empty, could hardly get off the couch, couldn’t enjoy my kids, and thought a lot about ending my life, down to where and how. But that deep sadness comes and goes; the strange beliefs, the smells, the speech problems, and the repetitive movements never really let up.
D007-D005_h012.options:
A. Anorexia Nervosa
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia

D007-D005_h013.question:

I don’t really see my friends anymore; I just don’t feel any pull to talk to people or go out.

D007-D005_h014.question:

I catch myself talking in rhymes or because a word sounds right, not because it fits.
